concepts.name: The exposure triangle
concepts.source_span: Three settings control exposure: aperture, shutter speed and ISO.

questions.stem: What is exposure in photography?
options: The amount of light that reaches the camera sensor
The number of photos on a memory card
The size of the final print
The colour of the camera body

questions.stem: Which three settings make up the exposure triangle?
What does a photo look like if too little light reaches the sensor?
What does a photo look like if too much light reaches the sensor?
Which of these is NOT one of the three exposure settings?

concepts.name: Aperture
concepts.source_span: A smaller f-number means a wider opening, so more light enters.

questions.stem: Which f-number lets in the most light?
What does a wide aperture give?
What does a narrow aperture give?
options: Both near and far objects sharp

questions.stem: What is aperture?
options: The time the shutter stays open
The size of the opening in the lens that lets light in

questions.stem: In what is aperture measured?

concepts.name: Shutter speed
concepts.source_span: A fast shutter speed freezes motion, as in a sports photo.

questions.stem: What does a fast shutter speed do to moving subjects?
What happens to moving objects at a slow shutter speed?
Which shutter speed is faster?
What is shutter speed?
options: How big the lens opening is
How long the sensor is exposed to light

questions.stem: What is a common guide for the slowest shutter speed when holding the camera by hand?
options: At least 1 over the focal length

concepts.name: ISO
concepts.source_span: A high ISO such as 3200 makes the photo brighter in the dark but adds noise, which looks like grain.

questions.stem: What does a high ISO do?
options: Makes the photo darker and sharper
Makes the photo brighter in the dark but adds noise

questions.stem: What does the noise in a high-ISO photo look like?
Which ISO gives the cleanest image if there is plenty of light?
What is ISO?
options: The size of the lens opening
The sensitivity of the sensor to light

questions.stem: When would you raise the ISO?
options: When you want a slower shutter

concepts.name: Stops
concepts.source_span: A stop is a doubling or halving of the amount of light.

questions.stem: What is a stop?
options: A doubling or halving of the amount of light
A button that stops the shutter

questions.stem: What happens if you open the aperture by one stop?
options: The same amount of light enters

questions.stem: Doubling the ISO from 200 to 400 makes the image:
Which sequence lists aperture stops from widest to narrowest?
If you use a faster shutter speed, how can you keep the same exposure?
options: Use a wider aperture or a higher ISO

concepts.name: Composition and light
concepts.source_span: Golden hour is the hour after sunrise and the hour before sunset, when the light is soft and warm.

questions.stem: What is golden hour?
options: The hour after sunrise and the hour before sunset

questions.stem: What kind of light does golden hour have?
What does the rule of thirds suggest?
options: Always putting the subject in the exact centre
Placing the subject along lines that divide the frame into three equal parts
Taking three photos of each scene

questions.stem: What does white balance do?
options: Adjusts colours so white objects look white under different lighting

questions.stem: Where can the subject be placed according to the rule of thirds?
options: At the crossings of the dividing lines
